questions.knowledge_point: Cases When a Square’s Side Is Mapped to a Segment
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ and its **directed** boundary $∂Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, where $Δ$ is given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=v-{u}^{2},\,y=u+v.
$$

The image of the side ${S}_{2}$ under the action of $T$ is a **directed** line segment. Find the endpoints of this segment, stated in the order that they are traversed.
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{2}.$

For the side ${S}_{2},$ we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(v-{u}^{2},\,u+v) \\  & =(v-{1}^{2},\,1+v) \\  & =(v-1,\,v+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{2}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=v-1,\,y=v+1,\,0\le v\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=t-1,\,y(t)=t+1,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

This is a line segment with endpoints $(-1,1)$ and $(0,2)$ in the $xy$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/f304c409cfc62de3d296690c0acd2cec5b9726c03d8a196ed69de36d8ebbefd2.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Cases When a Square’s Side Is Mapped to a Parabola
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x={u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,y=-v.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{2}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{2}.$

For the side ${S}_{2},$ we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,-v) \\  & =({1}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,-v) \\  & =({v}^{2}+1,\,-v).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{2}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x={v}^{2}+1,\,y=-v,\,0\le v\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x={t}^{2}+1,\,y=-t,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
x=(-y)^{2}+1\,⇒\,{y}^{2}=x-1
$$

which is a right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(1,0).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{2}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(1,0)\to ({1}^{2}+{0}^{2},-0)=(1,0) \\  & T:(1,1)\to ({1}^{2}+{1}^{2},-1)=(2,-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{2}$ is an arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(2,-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/ade48b3f14ed83460a5d818f744103edd75f8394a3f3396a0ff30364bda36c9b.png)

choices.value: An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,-1)$ to $(1,0).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,-1)$ to $(1,0).$
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(2,-1).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(2,-1).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,1)$ to $(2,1).$

answer_fields.correct_value: An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(2,-1).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Square
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/5f91cc8b30f9b764021cd84c374a328c7ffb1287a9f0dc6a211a3fadfac2fdbd.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=v(u+1),\,y={v}^{2}.
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$ 

*Hint: You may assume that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We're told that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$ So, to map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{1},$ where we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =(v(u+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(0(u+1),\,{0}^{2}) &  \\  & =(0,\,0), & 0\le u\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{2}.$ Here, we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =(v(u+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(v(1+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(2v,\,{v}^{2}), & 0\le v\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is an upward-opening parabola traversed from the point $(0,0)$ to the point $(2,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{3}.$ Here, we have $v=1$ and $1\ge u\ge 0.$ Substituting $v=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =(v(u+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(1(u+1),\,{1}^{2}) &  \\  & =(u+1,\,1), & 1\ge u\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a horizontal line segment traversed from the point $(2,1)$ to the point $(1,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{4}.$ Here, we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =(v(u+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(v(0+1),\,{v}^{2}) &  \\  & =(v,\,{v}^{2}), & 1\ge v\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

 
This is an upward-opening parabola traversed from the point $(1,1)$ to the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

Drawing the images of the sides of our square, we obtain the following image of $Δ:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/4a2614c282a7cd82ff52ecacd7135f9c95bce5df5cfa9a06f2824b63c60c6eb2.png)

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=u(v+1),\,y=4u(v-u).
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{3}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{3}.$

For the side ${S}_{3},$ we have $v=1$ and $1\ge u\ge 0.$ Substituting $v=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u(v+1),\,4u(v-u)) \\  & =(u(1+1),\,4u(1-u)) \\  & =(2u,\,4u(1-u)).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{3}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=2u,\,y=4u(1-u),\,1\ge u\ge 0.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=2t,\,y(t)=4t(1-t),\,1\ge t\ge 0.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
y=2x(1-\frac{x}{2})\,⇒\,y=-(x-1)^{2}+1
$$

which is a downward-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(1,1).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{3}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(1,1)\to ((1)(1+1),\,4(1)(1-1))=(2,0) \\  & T:(0,1)\to ((0)(1+1),\,4(0)(1-0))=(0,0)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{3}$ is an arc of a downward-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,0)$ to $(0,0).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096545/assets/970003245107516d9be7b4729d6c18abf01d1f48c82211402f06d13cec4e3a08.png)

An arc of a downward-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,0)$ to $(0,0).$
